sources.entry: LinkLiar - Keep your MAC address random for privacy (intuitive GUI for ifconfig)

summary.one_liner: LinkLiar is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app written in Swift that spoofs the MAC addresses of Wi-Fi and Ethernet interfaces, acting as a GUI over ifconfig.
summary.what_it_does: The app runs as a status menu item on macOS and changes the hardware MAC address of Wi-Fi (Airport) and Ethernet interfaces to a random or chosen value. It asks for administrator privileges once, then makes the change through ifconfig. The README says it can be configured to re-randomize the MAC address, and that it disassociates from a connected network first, since macOS 12.3 blocks MAC changes while connected. Advanced options are available by holding the Option key while the menu is open, and the README describes these as intended for developers. A logging mechanism is available through a log file that the app's components write to when it exists, and a bundled logs utility shows live debugging output. End-user documentation is hosted on the project's GitHub Pages site, and the README mentions a HelpBook generated with bin/docs.
use_cases: Keep a random MAC address for privacy on public Wi-Fi
Stop devices from leaking the hardware MAC address
Change a Mac's Wi-Fi or Ethernet MAC address without the Terminal
Debug MAC address changes with live logs
notable: GUI front end for ifconfig-based MAC address spoofing on macOS
Can re-randomize the MAC address on a schedule or after changes, per the README's caveat about re-randomizing
Bundled logs utility for live debugging output
Option-key menu reveals developer-only advanced options
caveats: Requires macOS Sierra (10.12) or later and administrator password once; Wi-Fi must be on to change its MAC address
Some hardware cannot change MAC: 2018 MacBooks are noted as blocked by a macOS bug
Changing the MAC on a connected interface briefly drops the connection; on macOS 12.3+ it disassociates from the network first
